intro.text: A number sign (#) is used with this entry because of evidence that osteogenesis imperfecta type XIII (OI13) is caused by homozygous or compound heterozygous mutation in the BMP1 gene (112264) on chromosome 8p21.

checks.claim: Osteogenesis imperfecta type XIII (OI13) is caused by homozygous or compound heterozygous mutation in the BMP1 gene.
checks.evidence_quote: we describe a mutation associated to severe AR-OI (OI type III) in an additional gene, BMP1, which extends further the list of genes that are mutated in this heterogeneous disorder.
checks.explanation: Paper reports only a homozygous mutation; compound heterozygous mutations are not described here.

checks.claim: The BMP1 gene is located on chromosome 8p21.
checks.evidence_quote: BMP1 and its longer isoform mammalian Tolloid protein (mTLD) are alternative spliced products of BMP1 (MIM# 112264), which is located on 8p21.3.
checks.explanation: 8p21.3 is within 8p21.

paragraphs.text: Osteogenesis imperfecta type XIII is an autosomal recessive form of OI caused by defective BMP1 (procollagen C-proteinase) activity. It is characterized by recurrent fractures and bone fragility. Unlike most other forms of OI, it is associated with normal or increased bone mineral density.

checks.claim: Osteogenesis imperfecta type XIII is an autosomal recessive form of OI.
checks.evidence_quote: We conclude that BMP1 is an additional gene mutated in AR-OI.
checks.explanation: Paper describes BMP1-related OI as autosomal recessive.

checks.claim: Osteogenesis imperfecta type XIII is caused by defective BMP1 (procollagen C-proteinase) activity.
checks.evidence_quote: proving that the Phe249Leu mutation leads to a BMP1/mTLD protein with deficient PICP proteolytic activity
checks.explanation: Paper shows deficient C-propeptide cleavage activity as the likely cause but does not use the 'type XIII' designation or the term 'procollagen C-proteinase'.

checks.claim: Osteogenesis imperfecta type XIII is characterized by recurrent fractures and bone fragility.
checks.evidence_quote: affected by increased bone mineral density and multiple recurrent fractures
checks.explanation: Recurrent fractures and bone fragility (title) are stated.

checks.claim: Unlike most other forms of OI, osteogenesis imperfecta type XIII is associated with normal or increased bone mineral density.
checks.evidence_quote: affected by increased bone mineral density and multiple recurrent fractures
checks.explanation: Increased BMD is stated, but the comparison with other OI forms and 'normal' BMD are not in the abstract.

paragraphs.text: Martinez-Glez et al. (2012) studied a consanguineous Egyptian family in which affected members had autosomal recessive OI with recurrent fractures and, unusually for OI, increased bone mineral density.

checks.claim: Martinez-Glez et al. (2012) studied a consanguineous Egyptian family with OI.
checks.evidence_quote: Herein, we have studied a consanguineous Egyptian family with two children diagnosed with severe autosomal recessive osteogenesis imperfecta (AR-OI)

checks.claim: Affected members of the consanguineous Egyptian family studied by Martinez-Glez et al. (2012) had autosomal recessive OI with recurrent fractures.
checks.evidence_quote: Recurrent fractures of both upper and lower limbs occurred with an average rate of 15/year.
checks.explanation: Both siblings had AR-OI with recurrent fractures.

checks.claim: Affected members of the consanguineous Egyptian family studied by Martinez-Glez et al. (2012) had increased bone mineral density, which is unusual for OI.
checks.evidence_quote: Bone densitometry (DEXA) at 5 years revealed borderline osteoporosis at the spine (Z-score −1.63) and osteoporosis at the left femur (Z-score −2.75).
checks.explanation: Paper reports decreased bone density and osteoporosis in both patients, not increased BMD.

paragraphs.text: Asharani et al. (2012) described affected sibs from a consanguineous family who had severe bone fragility with multiple fractures. Bone mineral density was increased.

checks.claim: Asharani et al. (2012) described affected sibs from a consanguineous family.
checks.evidence_quote: in a consanguineous family affected by increased bone mineral density and multiple recurrent fractures
checks.explanation: A consanguineous family is stated; the abstract does not say the affected individuals were sibs.

checks.claim: The affected sibs described by Asharani et al. (2012) had severe bone fragility with multiple fractures.
checks.evidence_quote: affected by increased bone mineral density and multiple recurrent fractures
checks.explanation: Multiple fractures and bone fragility are stated; 'severe' and 'sibs' are not in the abstract.

checks.claim: The affected sibs described by Asharani et al. (2012) had increased bone mineral density.
checks.evidence_quote: in a consanguineous family affected by increased bone mineral density
checks.explanation: Increased BMD is stated.

paragraphs.text: The transmission pattern of OI13 in the families reported by Martinez-Glez et al. (2012) and Asharani et al. (2012) fit autosomal recessive inheritance.

checks.claim: The transmission pattern of OI13 in the family reported by Martinez-Glez et al. (2012) fit autosomal recessive inheritance.
checks.evidence_quote: Segregation analysis of the mutation within the family showed the two affected children to be homozygous for the c.747C>G nucleotide change, while the normal sister (II-2) and brother (II-4) from whom DNA was available and the parents carried the mutation in the heterozygous state.

checks.claim: The transmission pattern of OI13 in the family reported by Asharani et al. (2012) fit autosomal recessive inheritance.
checks.evidence_quote: we found a homozygous causative BMP1 mutation, c.34G>C, in a consanguineous family
checks.explanation: Consistent with autosomal recessive inheritance, but the abstract does not say so explicitly.

paragraphs.text: In affected members of a consanguineous Egyptian family with OI13, Martinez-Glez et al. (2012) identified a homozygous missense mutation in the BMP1 gene (F249L). It affected the protease domain. Functional studies showed that BMP1/mTLD proteolytic activity was deficient, with impaired processing of the type I procollagen C-propeptide.

checks.claim: Martinez-Glez et al. (2012) identified a homozygous missense mutation in the BMP1 gene (F249L) in affected members of a consanguineous Egyptian family with OI13.
checks.evidence_quote: found a homozygous c.747C>G nucleotide change in exon 6 that causes the substitution of phenylalanine at position 249 to leucine (p.Phe249Leu)

checks.claim: The BMP1 F249L mutation affects the protease domain.
checks.evidence_quote: Mutation analysis identified both patients with a Phe249Leu homozygous missense change within the BMP1 protease domain

checks.claim: Functional studies by Martinez-Glez et al. (2012) showed that BMP1/mTLD proteolytic activity was deficient with the BMP1 F249L mutation.
checks.evidence_quote: thus indicating that the Phe249Leu mutation causes strong reduction of the BMP1/mTLD proteolytic function and confirming the pathogenicity of the mutation
checks.explanation: Paper shows deficient activity, but described as a strong reduction; patient cells retained some residual cleavage, which may come from the mutant enzyme or from other proteases in the culture.

checks.claim: Functional studies by Martinez-Glez et al. (2012) showed impaired processing of the type I procollagen C-propeptide with the BMP1 F249L mutation.
checks.evidence_quote: Type I procollagen analysis in supernatants from cultured fibroblasts demonstrated abnormal PICP processing in patient-derived cells consistent with the mutation causing decreased BMP1 function.

paragraphs.text: Asharani et al. (2012) identified a homozygous missense mutation in the BMP1 gene (G12R) in affected sibs with OI13. The mutation lay in the signal peptide. The authors linked this finding to the zebrafish 'frilly fins' (frf) mutant, which carries bmp1a mutations. That mutant showed defective procollagen C-terminal processing and abnormal bone formation, and the human mutation was shown to reduce BMP1 function.

checks.claim: Asharani et al. (2012) identified a homozygous missense mutation in the BMP1 gene (G12R) in affected sibs with OI13.
checks.evidence_quote: we found a homozygous causative BMP1 mutation, c.34G>C, in a consanguineous family
checks.explanation: The abstract gives c.34G>C only; the protein change G12R and the word 'sibs' are not stated.

checks.claim: The BMP1 G12R mutation lies in the signal peptide.
checks.evidence_quote: The mutation is located within the BMP1 signal peptide
checks.explanation: Stated directly.

checks.claim: The zebrafish 'frilly fins' (frf) mutant carries bmp1a mutations.
checks.evidence_quote: We also characterize a zebrafish bone mutant harboring lesions in bmp1a
checks.explanation: The bmp1a mutant is stated; the 'frilly fins' name is not in the abstract.

checks.claim: The zebrafish 'frilly fins' mutant showed defective procollagen C-terminal processing and abnormal bone formation.
checks.evidence_quote: Bmp1a is critically required for mature-collagen generation, downstream of osteoblast maturation, in bone
checks.explanation: Defective collagen maturation and bone defects are implied; procollagen C-terminal processing is not explicitly stated.

checks.claim: Asharani et al. (2012) showed that the human BMP1 G12R mutation reduces BMP1 function.
checks.evidence_quote: The mutation is located within the BMP1 signal peptide and leads to impaired secretion and an alteration in posttranslational modification.
checks.explanation: Impaired secretion, together with the title's 'Attenuated BMP1 function', supports reduced function.

paragraphs.text: Asharani et al. (2012) showed that zebrafish 'frilly fins' mutants carry mutations in bmp1a. The mutants had defective procollagen I C-propeptide processing and disorganized collagen fibrils, together with abnormal fin and bone development and increased bone density.

checks.claim: Asharani et al. (2012) showed that zebrafish 'frilly fins' mutants carry mutations in bmp1a.
checks.evidence_quote: We also characterize a zebrafish bone mutant harboring lesions in bmp1a
checks.explanation: The 'frilly fins' name is not given in the abstract.

checks.claim: Zebrafish 'frilly fins' bmp1a mutants had defective procollagen I C-propeptide processing.
checks.evidence_quote: Bmp1a is critically required for mature-collagen generation, downstream of osteoblast maturation, in bone
checks.explanation: Mature collagen generation is stated; procollagen I C-propeptide processing is not specified in the abstract.

checks.claim: Zebrafish 'frilly fins' bmp1a mutants had disorganized collagen fibrils.
checks.explanation: Disorganized collagen fibrils are not mentioned in the abstract.

checks.claim: Zebrafish 'frilly fins' bmp1a mutants had abnormal fin and bone development.
checks.evidence_quote: We also characterize a zebrafish bone mutant harboring lesions in bmp1a, demonstrating conservation of BMP1 function in osteogenesis across species.
checks.explanation: A bone defect is stated; abnormal fin development is not mentioned in the abstract.

checks.claim: Zebrafish 'frilly fins' bmp1a mutants had increased bone density.
checks.explanation: The abstract reports increased BMD only in the human family, not in the zebrafish mutants.

paragraphs.text: In affected members of a consanguineous Egyptian family with OI13 and increased bone mineral density, Martinez-Glez et al. (2012) identified a homozygous phe249-to-leu (F249L) mutation in the BMP1 gene. Functional studies showed that the mutation reduced BMP1 proteolytic activity, including processing of the procollagen C-propeptide.

checks.claim: Martinez-Glez et al. (2012) identified a homozygous phe249-to-leu (F249L) mutation in the BMP1 gene in affected members of a consanguineous Egyptian family with OI13.
checks.evidence_quote: Mutation analysis identified both patients with a Phe249Leu homozygous missense change within the BMP1 protease domain

checks.claim: Affected members of the consanguineous Egyptian family with the homozygous BMP1 F249L mutation had increased bone mineral density.
checks.evidence_quote: and generalized decreased bone density (Fig. 1B–G)
checks.explanation: Patients had decreased bone density and borderline osteoporosis to osteoporosis, not increased BMD.

checks.claim: Functional studies showed that the BMP1 F249L mutation reduced BMP1 proteolytic activity, including processing of the procollagen C-propeptide.
checks.evidence_quote: proving that the Phe249Leu mutation leads to a BMP1/mTLD protein with deficient PICP proteolytic activity
checks.explanation: Reduced activity and impaired C-propeptide processing are shown, but the claim's 'including' implies other substrates were tested; only procollagen I C-propeptide processing was tested, and other substrates are only suggested in the discussion.

paragraphs.text: In affected sibs from a consanguineous family with OI13, Asharani et al. (2012) identified a homozygous gly12-to-arg (G12R) mutation in the signal peptide of BMP1. The affected sibs had multiple fractures and increased bone mineral density. Functional studies showed that the mutation reduced BMP1 function.

checks.claim: Asharani et al. (2012) identified a homozygous gly12-to-arg (G12R) mutation in the signal peptide of BMP1 in affected sibs from a consanguineous family with OI13.
checks.evidence_quote: we found a homozygous causative BMP1 mutation, c.34G>C, in a consanguineous family
checks.explanation: Homozygous signal-peptide mutation in a consanguineous family is stated; the G12R protein notation and 'sibs' are not in the abstract.

checks.claim: The sibs with the homozygous BMP1 G12R mutation had multiple fractures.
checks.evidence_quote: affected by increased bone mineral density and multiple recurrent fractures
checks.explanation: Stated.

checks.claim: The sibs with the homozygous BMP1 G12R mutation had increased bone mineral density.
checks.evidence_quote: affected by increased bone mineral density and multiple recurrent fractures
checks.explanation: Stated.

checks.claim: Functional studies showed that the BMP1 G12R mutation reduced BMP1 function.
checks.evidence_quote: The mutation is located within the BMP1 signal peptide and leads to impaired secretion and an alteration in posttranslational modification.
checks.explanation: Functional findings of impaired secretion support reduced function.
